name: Jackal
otherStatistics: Perception +3. Passive Perception 13. No listed languages or special senses.
appearance: A slim sandy canid with tall pointed ears, a narrow muzzle, a dark saddle along the back, and a bushy tail.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, D&D Basic Rules v1.0, 2018 , Chapter 12, Monsters, p. 141.
sections.Traits:
Keen Hearing and Smell. Wisdom (Perception) checks using hearing or smell have advantage.
Pack Tactics. The jackal has advantage on an attack roll against a creature when an ally of the jackal within 5 ft. of that creature is not incapacitated.
sections.Actions: Bite. Melee weapon attack, +1 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 1 (1d4 − 1) piercing damage.
sections.At the table: Use passive Perception 13 normally and 18 for a passive check that relies on hearing or smell. Pack Tactics takes no action.

name: Rhinoceros
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Passive Perception 11. No listed languages, skill bonuses, or special senses.
appearance: A stocky gray rhinoceros with folds of thick skin, two horns above the snout, and short, sturdy legs.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, D&D Basic Rules v1.0, 2018 , Chapter 12, Monsters, p. 151.
sections.Traits: Charge. Move at least 20 ft. straight toward a target and hit it with Gore on the same turn. The hit deals an extra 9 (2d8) bludgeoning damage. If the target is a creature, it also makes a DC 15 Strength save or falls prone.
sections.Actions: Gore. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 14 (2d8 + 5) bludgeoning damage.
sections.At the table: The charge damage is added on a hit. The save decides whether the target falls prone. A prone creature has disadvantage on attack rolls and can crawl or spend half its speed to stand. Attacks against it have advantage from within 5 ft. and disadvantage from farther away.
